scope: Heartbeat-only best-effort teacher private reply recovery within the final mandatory authority transaction.

source.state: incremental uncommitted shared worktree; final application/test files
source.note: Archive-time hashes describe final files; early runs predate additional assertions/type-only corrections. Combined clean-source CI and capacity acceptance remain separate.

behavior.before: Recovery-due heartbeats acquired an extra tenant lease and full authority transaction before performing final HTTP authority checks.
behavior.after: One final lease/transaction performs mandatory SSO/Focus/control preparation, then optional recovery in a savepoint with mandatory exact-binding fences. Redis promises have immediate rejection handlers and settle after lease release. Default and WebSocket callers retain their mandatory claim behavior.
behavior.failureSemantics: Optional lifecycle-latch, claim SQL or synchronous socket failure does not fail an otherwise valid heartbeat. Required authorization, preparation, binding-query failures and failed savepoint rollback/release still fail closed.

nativeFixture.isolation: Each attempt created a fresh uniquely labeled local Docker PostgreSQL container with loopback-only random port and removed it after both runs. Read-only schema export from local synthetic donor; no production mutations.
nativeFixture.ordinary: Application queries use fixture owner; this does not prove RLS.
nativeFixture.restricted: Application queries use separate NOSUPERUSER NOBYPASSRLS NOINHERIT role with RLS_GUC_ENABLED and lifecycle admission inventory; separate owner URL used only for fixture setup, writer races, assertions and cleanup.
nativeFixture.resources: 2 CPUs,2GiB local fixture; test correctness only, no capacity claim.

Optional lifecycle latch failure preserves valid HTTP but never stale binding authority
Required preparation and exact-binding SQL faults propagate; manual lease expiry prevents both emissions
Binding transfer rejects old optional recovery and allows current exact binding
Competing SSO writer exercised against bootstrap and consolidated heartbeat
Existing lifecycle close/send/ACK/hard-off/reconnect and Redis integrity tests retained
Actual route slice checks raw control revision, exact frames, immediate Redis rejection handling and lease release before network settlement
limitations: Focused route tests execute the actual source slice with bounded fakes; native storage/relay/WebSocket tests exercise PostgreSQL and actual sockets, not the complete HTTP server.
No full-load success or deployment readiness claim. Source-run native tests avoid shared dist rebuild while parallel owners were editing.
A best-effort partial local send can precede a rolled-back optional claim; stable IDs and mandatory relay lifecycle/binding checks remain the existing retry/deduplication boundary.
sanitation: Database URLs, JWT-shaped values and user-home paths are redacted. Raw schema/runner environment secrets are not included. Original hashes and all failed attempts retained.
